statements.text: Asteroids are rocky bodies that mostly orbit the Sun between Mars and Jupiter; comets are icy bodies that can grow a bright tail when they come close to the Sun.
Comets show long bright tails throughout every part of their orbits around the Sun.
Every asteroid must orbit strictly between Mars and Jupiter; none can be found on any other path around the Sun.

stem: Advik sorts notes about asteroids and comets by shape, composition, position, tail, and motion around the Sun.

teacher.key_rationale: Asteroids are mainly rocky and many lie between Mars and Jupiter; comets are icy and grow tails near the Sun, not all along the orbit. Not every asteroid is confined to that belt.
